slides.label: WHY REVIEWS DECIDE BOOKINGS
lines: Elk hunts are expensive, rare and hard to undo. Hunters look for proof before they trust you.
A happy hunter rarely leaves a review on their own. Asking is the only thing that fixes that.

slides.label: SET IT UP ONCE
slides.title: 20 minutes, three steps
items: In your Google Business Profile, open “Ask for reviews” and copy the short link. Test it on your phone.
Turn it into a QR code
Paste the link into any free QR generator. Print it on a card for the gear bag or camp wall.
Save the message in your phone
One text you can send in two minutes after each hunt.

slides.label: THE MESSAGE
slides.sub: Text it two or three days after the hunt.
slides.subject: Thank you from camp
body: Hey [first name], hope you're settled back in. It was a pleasure having you in camp.
If you've got a minute, a quick Google review helps other hunters find us. If you want to mention which hunt you were on and who guided you, that's what other hunters look for: [your link]

slides.label: RUN IT EVERY HUNT
rows: Hand them the QR card. One sentence: “this helps other hunters find us.”
Send the text. Email too if that's all you have.

slides.label: THE RULES THAT KEEP YOU OUT OF TROUBLE
items: Not only the hunters you think were happy.
Never offer a discount or gift
A hunt went sideways? Call first
Then send the same message everyone gets.
They can still have had a great trip. Ask them too.

slides.label: THEN REPLY TO EVERY REVIEW
lines: Answer within a couple of days, with their first name and one specific detail.
Hunters reading a bad review care more about how you responded than what it said.
